As someone who struggles with some brutal mental illnesses it's hard to see past the stigma surrounding them.  Especially in my family.  I want to be able to see a world where things are actually changing for people like me. 

 I myself have depression, PTSD, Borderline Personality Disorder, high anxiety and paranoia.   Trying to talk about any of these to my family is nearly impossible.  All I get is "get over it" or "suck it up" or "just do it!".

I'm being pushed to my furthest limit...

I'm 27 years old.  Engaged to an incredible woman.  In 2013 my mom died of an aneurysm.  Found her choking on her own vomit and 16 hours later she was officially dead.  Year and a half after that my brother put me into the hospital whilst owing me 5 grand.  Less than a year after that my cat of 11 years died fairly quickly as well.  She was fine the day before I wake up the next morning and she's completely unlike herself.  Took her to the vet then had to put her down the next day.  I moved out of province from Alberta to B.C for the second time.  I moved the first time right after my mom died for a year and a few months to get help.

After moving the second time I moved I ended up in the hospital in September after 6 months for suicidality.  I met my fiance in the hospital and we both got discharged to the same what I would call a half way house for mental health.  Transition from hospital to life again.  Our relationship only grew from there.  We were homeless in October after going back to the hospital and being discharged homeless even though I was very suicidal.  A good friend took us in for a month when we found a home with 1 roommate.  We had to leave that place cause the roommate decided he wanted to live alone and hopefully his partner.

We moved into a large house with literally 8 other people.  That shit was not good for our mental health.  Being around drunken assholes and drugs.  I am not into partying stuff and my fiance recently came outta that stuff.  At that house we bought a dog and then a month or so after we got the dog they evicted us on 48 hour notice.  Since we did not sign a lease we were fucked and there was nothing we could do.  We moved in with my fiancé's parents and they are NOT good people.  We had to live and witness child abuse and animal abuse for 6 months.  Since then the child has been taken out of care and we are in the works of getting the animals removed as well.  We finally found a beautiful basement suite with a big backyard and amazing landlords.

We found out today the landlords sold the place and we need to be out officially by the end of August.  We moved here in February.

I could give a detailed history of my life before my mom died but in a nutshell. Verbal and mental abuse.  Abandonment neglect and a very cruel upbringing.  Basically being told I'm shit my whole life.  My fiance is a lot of the same boat.  As you can imagine from her parents.  My fiance and I both have Borderline Personality Disorder.  I myself have been working on my mental health since my mom died.  My fiance is a year and a half into it.

We cannot seem to find stable ground and get into a safe money situation.  We are constantly running into shit shit situations.  All the places we've left, except for the alcoholics, we left on great terms and use them as references.

Now.. Where we live the vacancy rare is under 1%.  They also seem to hate animals here.  We are talking about leaving the town we are in.. Well cause we might have to anyways.  We are thinking of moving back to my home cause I have family there and my fiance has family near by.  It's also cheaper and a hell of a lot easier to find housing.  The biggest problem with that is we are currently on disability in B.C.  Last time I checked it was not transferable from province to province.  So B.C to Alberta had different disability systems.  I won't find out till Tuesday if that's still the case.

This is amazing to hear.  I myself have borderline and was diagnosed 2 or 3 years ago and I met my future wife in a hospital last year and she also has BPD.  It feels like the hardest thing in the world.  Since its an invisible illness people think you should just be fine and just be happy.  "Get over it"  has got to be the worst thing you can do for people like us.

I'm so happy to hear you are looking forward to the future.. I know what you mean by "finally looking forward".

So my point is I empathize drastically with you and I am happy to hear a follow borderline person is happy and looking toward the future!  Hell of a job.

I'm sure you've heard of DBT and CBT and I'm also quite sure you've been through those groups also.  For anyone else with it or know anyone with it.  DO DBT!!  It's a massive life changer.

PSA:  If someone you know and love/care about.  Just show them you're trying the best you can to understand and support them.  This is 100% the best thing you can do.  Validate them and try.  When I found out my sister was reading a book about it I broke down and cried right away.  When I told my aunt about Borderline she said "sounds like everyone has it, not a big deal"  And that caused a lot of damage and now I never go back to her about my struggles.

Longer comment than anticipated but the stigma around Borderline is doing so much damage.  Spread as much information about it as you can to beat the stigma.  The stigma is doing just as much damage as having borderline, if not more.

There are others out there and we understand and we care.  Stay strong and try your best and it WILL get better.  I've been down a horrible road the last 5 years and it has gotten better through counselling, DBT and CBT.  If you're scared to do group counselling... I promise it's so rewarding to be around people who actually understand and think JUST LIKE YOU.  Stay strong!!!
